source.title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
source.authors: Fabian Gröger; Shuo Wen; Maria Brbic

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-modal representation alignment and its scaling with a different measurement approach: permutation-calibrated similarity metrics.
record.gate_note: Cited convergence results from prior work are not recorded as findings. The study's own model-comparison results, calibration comparisons, and parameter-sensitivity results are included. Results about calibration performance unrelated to representation alignment are omitted.
record.test_reason: Re-runs the Huh et al. PRH protocol (WIT n=1024, same LLM and vision families, max over layers) with permutation null-calibration. It argues the global-convergence form of V1/V2 is a width/depth artifact and restates it as local-neighbourhood convergence. It also extends the test to video–text.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that raw global spectral and geometric convergence is largely confounded by width and depth and mostly disappears after calibration. Local neighbourhood alignment, but not local distances (small-σ CKA-RBF), remains significant and tracks capability across image–text and video–text. They propose the Aristotelian hypothesis, convergence to shared local neighbourhood relationships, as a refinement that the Platonic hypothesis implies, not a refutation.
record.recipe_differences: Follows the image–text comparison protocol of Huh et al. (2024), including layerwise similarity and maximum summaries, but adds permutation-based scalar and aggregation-aware calibration and compares several metric families.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on metric family: calibrated global metrics lose their scale trend while neighborhood metrics retain it. The trend varies with neighborhood size k and RBF bandwidth σ; it is strongest at small k, absent for CKA-RBF at σ=0.1, and flatter at larger k or σ. The study also tests α values of 0.01, 0.05, and 0.10 and reports the qualitative pattern is unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: All 204 vision–language pairs show cross-modal similarity significantly above a permutation null (most p≈0.002), for both local and global metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal vision–language alignment exceeds chance in every tested pair, regardless of model scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The study states that representational similarity has no ground-truth scale and therefore its calibrated evidence does not prove convergence. Results on model scaling are cross-modal comparisons rather than a controlled intervention on model capability. Several model-pair findings are presented as aggregate correlations or figures, without uncertainty estimates for the reported correlations. The exchangeability guarantee may require restricted permutations for grouped or dependent samples.
record.rows_left_out: Not stated; 26 rows retained, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Only vision–language (and video–language) pairs are tested. There are no same-modality cross-architecture comparisons. The capability axis is mainly language-model rank/BPB.
Only WIT images (n=1024) and PVD videos are used; other paired datasets and caption sources are not tested.
Out-of-distribution inputs and different input sets are not tested; dependence is shown on metric family, k, σ, width and depth only.
The causal part is not tested: whether shared data or objectives, rather than a model of reality, explain alignment. Absolute completeness of alignment is not quantified.

missing.what: Calibrated mKNN plateaus for larger models at k=100 (raw plateaus too), while the k=10 trend persists. Bears on V7 plateau.
SVCCA loses its scaling trend after calibration (DINOv2 subset); no number is given in Table 2.
The local–global divergence replicates on a continuous BPB language-performance axis.
Frame-level DINOv2/CLIP and non-finetuned VideoMAE versus LLMs on PVD show the same pattern.
On real DINOv2/AugReg pairs at fixed n=1024, the permutation threshold grows with width (r=0.88).
Absolute calibrated alignment magnitudes are small (e.g. mKNN calibrated roughly 0.05–0.2); these bear on how far alignment is from complete.

record.verdict_notes: T5 because the study re-runs the original PRH protocol to argue V1/V2 must be restated as local-only convergence. For V7 the cause part is untested; the authors explicitly say they do not contradict shared-data or objective explanations. Rows r25 and r26 are synthetic and partly validate the authors' own method; they are kept only for raw-metric inflation (V6). Correlations are computed with language-model rank, not a controlled scale intervention, and carry no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests scaling of cross-modal alignment across the evaluated model families, not every combination of architectures, objectives, training data, or modalities.
Tests image–text and video–text alignment; does not establish generalization to all vision and language models or paired-data settings.
No comparisons of independently initialized seeds of the same architecture.
No tests of representation mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No tests of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests several metrics and neighborhood-size and RBF-bandwidth settings; does not test out-of-distribution inputs.
Shows that alignment is metric-dependent and incomplete or plateaus in some settings. Does not test whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause alignment.

relation.reason: Its own calibrated image–text and video–text experiments directly test convergence and its dependence on measurement choices.

tranche.reason: The study directly argues that global convergence evidence is confounded and restates the hypothesis in terms of local neighborhood relationships.

source_check.notes: Global alignment can remain statistically significant while its capability trend weakens or disappears; Section E.8 explicitly distinguishes these. V7's training-data/objective explanation is untested, and synthetic rows establish measurement confounding rather than trained-model convergence.

statements.correction: Table 2: calibrated neighborhood correlations at k=10,20,50 are 0.82–0.87. Section E.10: mKNN k=10 retains a clear upward trend; k=100 plateaus for larger models. No completeness or training-cause test is reported for these rows.
statements.problem: The correlations are correct, but they do not establish absence of a plateau for every neighborhood metric at k≤50 or qualify V7's incompleteness and causal claims.

statements.correction: Table 2: strong calibrated neighborhood capability correlations at k=10,20,50. Section E.10: clear continuing mKNN trend at k=10; flattening at large k.
statements.problem: Continuing small-k trends are supported, but absence of plateaus across all neighborhood metrics at k≤50 is stronger than the reported evidence.

statements.correction: Linear CKA: 0.86→0.45; unbiased CKA: 0.65→−0.01; mKNN k=10: 0.85→0.84. Small-k mKNN retains a clear scaling trend. Tested RBF bandwidths 0.5,2.0,5.0 flatten after calibration.
statements.problem: The numerical and publication claims are correct; the blanket small-k no-plateau claim and V7-against coverage overstate what the correlations establish.

reader_labels.condition: Calibrated global metrics in the tested image–text model families
reader_labels.reason: Global metric correlations with capability fall substantially after calibration, and the authors report no systematic calibrated increase with scale (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Calibrated local neighborhood metrics in the tested image–text model families
reader_labels.reason: Capability correlations remain high after calibration across tested neighborhood measures and k settings (r6–r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Calibrated local alignment strengthens with video-encoder capability, but smaller encoders bottleneck alignment and calibrated CKA has no capacity trend (r23–r24).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Global alignment magnitude loses its systematic scaling trend after calibration, although the tested pairs can still be statistically significant (r1–r5, r19).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Image–text local neighborhood alignment across tested model families and scales
reader_labels.reason: Calibrated neighborhood measures retain capability correlations and permutation-significant alignment (r6–r17, r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Local alignment increases with video-encoder capacity, but small encoders can limit it; global CKA has no capacity trend (r23–r24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Metric choice and local-similarity settings in the evaluated image–text data
reader_labels.reason: Global and neighborhood metrics behave differently after calibration; changing neighborhood size and RBF bandwidth changes the observed trend, including no significant calibrated alignment at σ=0.1 (r1–r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Alignment measured by global geometry or exact local distances, and broad-neighborhood settings
reader_labels.reason: The global scaling trend is not retained after calibration, exact local-distance alignment is absent at σ=0.1, and some broader-neighborhood trends flatten or weaken (r1–r5, r17, r20–r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Video results separate local alignment that strengthens with encoder capability from global CKA without a capacity trend, and report a bottleneck for smaller encoders (r23–r24).
